newsitem.title: CANADA: RIGEL ENERGY SEEN AS TAKEOVER TARGET.
newsitem.headline: RIGEL ENERGY SEEN AS TAKEOVER TARGET.

text.p: Rigel Energy Corp, which on Friday reported weaker first-half results and lowered expectations for the full year, may be in the sights of a potential acquisitor, industry sources said.
Rigel, which reported declines in production, cash flow and revenues for the first six months of 1997, had been widely speculated as a takeover target before its May annual meeting.
Its stock jumped after the meeting when Chief Executive Don West told shareholders about what could be a huge North Sea oil discovery, but has since fallen back from its highs.

Several sources said Talisman Energy Inc, no stranger to big acquisitions, was rumored to be taking a look at Rigel. Talisman spokesman Dave Mann said on Friday he did not know if that was indeed the case.
Mann said he could also not confirm talk that Talisman was on the restricted list of a Canadian brokerage.
West told Reuters on Friday that Talisman Chief Executive Jim Buckee had expressed interest in Rigel in the past but knew of no bid currently in the works.

The companies operate in similar regions in Canada and Talisman recently acquired more acreage in the Moray Firth area of the U.K. North Sea, where Rigel has 20 percent of what could be a major oil discovery operated by BG Plc.
"I've talked to Jim Buckee -- I know Jim pretty well -- and he's interested. But whether he would do a hostile, i kind of doubt it. But that's my own opinion," West said.

West said Rigel's North Sea position alone would not be enough to convince Talisman to bid for his company, which at Friday's share price of 14.45 would be valued at C$812 million based on 55.2 million shares outstanding. Friday's price, 0.05 on the day, was down from a year high of 17.70.
Rigel also had C$151 million in long-term debt at the end of the second quarter.

"We are a 20 percent interest holder in that property. Talisman getting another 20 percent with BG and Amerada (Hess Corp ) isn't going to do Talisman any good. They're trying for control and we're a minor player," he said.
West said his company's current share price was "not close" to his view of the value of the company, based on its potential for big increases in production.

The company on Friday announced a second-quarter net loss of C$1.2 million or C2 cents a share, down from net income of C$1.7 million or C3 cents a share in the same period last year. Cash flow was C$26.2 million or C47 cents a share, down from C$33.4 million or C60 cents a share.

Hit by the same shortages of drilling rigs and oil services that hammered several Canadian oil companies last quarter, as well as a sale last year, Rigel's oil production fell to 12,213 barrels a day from 14,855 and gas output dropped to 141.9 million cubic feet a day from 165.1 million.
Rigel said it was pursuing various promising drilling projects in the second half of the year, but they may be too late to allow it to meet its previous 1997 projections.

Peters & Co analyst Craig Langpap said he was skeptical of the takeover rumor because Rigel had been talked up as a target for a long time. "My speculation (of why the rumor intensified) was because the shares remained strong in light of what was clearly a disappointing quarter," Langpap said.
Talisman is near the top of the potential suitor list whenever talk in Canada's oil patch turns to takeovers.

The company was also speculated to be looking at Northstar Energy Corp , whose own stock price has faltered since its takeover early this year of Morrison Petroleums. Talisman was said to have examined Morrison, sources said, but instead launched its ill-fated hostile bid for Wascana Energy Inc. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
